provenance: Primary pages were retrieved and read by the parent research context. Report compiler consumed the shared search log, evidence matrix and source details; no independent second retrieval or human-read attestation is claimed.

sources.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
sources.version_note: Uses original arXiv year; ICLR 2023 publication is not used to relabel the 2022 preprint year.
sources.claim: Interleaving reasoning and actions allows plans to incorporate external observations.
sources.method_and_setting: Language-model reasoning and tool-action tasks; this review does not extract comparable banking outcome rates.
sources.limitation: Does not establish transaction authorization safety or banking effectiveness.
sources.design_implication: Separate candidate planning from trusted permissions and execution.

sources.title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
sources.claim: Stateful outcomes and repeated reliability matter; final database correctness can still miss required confirmation.
sources.method_and_setting: Tool-agent-user interactions in retail and airline domains; no reproduction in this project.
sources.limitation: Not a banking benchmark; original model rankings do not characterize this offline prototype.
sources.design_implication: Check final business state and authorization process separately; repeat future live-model trials.

sources.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
sources.claim: Benign utility, utility under attack and attacker-goal success are distinct evaluation axes.
sources.method_and_setting: Stateful tool-agent environment with prompt-injection tasks and defenses; project does not claim benchmark reproduction.
sources.limitation: Public attacks do not exhaust adversarial behaviors or prove general defense.
sources.design_implication: Measure actual side effects under attack while preserving legitimate task checks.

sources.title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Model Agents
sources.claim: External tool text can carry indirect injections aimed at harm or exfiltration.
sources.method_and_setting: Tool-integrated language-model attack benchmark; no original attack-rate transfer to this project.
sources.limitation: Specific historical prompts, tools and model results are not current-system rates.
sources.design_implication: Treat transaction notes, documents and tool output as untrusted data; test forged authorization parameters.

sources.title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design
sources.claim: Model-external control/data-flow handling and capability policies can define protection boundaries.
sources.method_and_setting: CaMeL design and evaluation under its own assumptions; detailed interpreter is not reproduced here.
sources.limitation: Project has no complete CaMeL interpreter, taint system or inherited formal guarantee.
sources.design_implication: Use a smaller trusted permission service and restricted numerical language; verify locally.

sources.title: Indirect Prompt Injections: Are Firewalls All You Need, or Stronger Benchmarks?
sources.claim: Weak attacks and evaluation limitations may inflate defense estimates; adaptive attacks remain relevant.
sources.method_and_setting: Prompt-injection firewall and benchmark assessment in the cited version; no numerical result imported.
sources.limitation: ArXiv version used; formal publication status not inferred.
sources.design_implication: Disclose fixed-suite scope and do not interpret zero observed violations as general safety.

sources.title: Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction
locators: These guidelines are validated through multiple rounds of evaluation
sources.claim: The paper proposes and evaluates human-AI interaction guidance across AI-product contexts.
sources.method_and_setting: Official summary reports evaluation with design practitioners and AI products; PDF not read in this review.
sources.limitation: No unverified guideline numbers or project user-benefit claims are extracted.
sources.design_implication: Make limitations and correction controls visible; test actual user effects later.

sources.title: Getting started with AIR
sources.claim: UK help documents conversational spending, subscription and some in-app actions, with gradual availability.
sources.method_and_setting: Short official product help page, not an independent product experiment.
sources.limitation: No universal regional availability, launch date or independent capability comparison inferred.
sources.design_implication: Connect analysis to actions while making authorization and receipts inspectable.

sources.title: Transaction Authorization Cheat Sheet
sources.claim: Enforce authorization server-side, preserve sequence, bind transaction data and invalidate prior authorization after changes.
sources.method_and_setting: Security guidance rather than an effectiveness study or legal compliance certification.
sources.limitation: Does not establish legal compliance or prove this implementation correct.
sources.design_implication: Bind confirmation/OTP to immutable user-operation parameters and recheck cumulative limits at commit.

sources.title: sqlite3 — DB-API 2.0 interface for SQLite databases
sources.claim: The Python sqlite3 interface exposes transaction control.
sources.method_and_setting: Official library semantics; local runtime version is recorded separately in evaluation artifacts.
sources.limitation: No claim of cross-database distributed atomicity or local code correctness.
sources.design_implication: Commit bank ledger, balances and receipts in one bank transaction and reconcile workflow recovery by operation ID.

sources.title: Job Objects
sources.claim: Job Objects support process/resource controls; process security restrictions are a separate concern.
sources.limitation: Resource limits alone do not provide filesystem/network isolation or arbitrary-code safety.
sources.design_implication: Combine process resource caps with a numerical DSL that has no I/O operations, and state the boundary explicitly.
